questions.q: Why does Carrow Mutual designate the core banking platform, not Salesforce, as the system of record for account balances and transactions?
options: Because Salesforce cannot technically store numeric financial data
Because that platform is the regulator-audited authoritative source for anything touching actual money movement
Because advisors never need to see balance data while working in Salesforce
Because the core banking platform is newer than Salesforce
questions.explain: The core banking platform is the system the regulator audits for balances and transactions, which makes it non-negotiably the system of record for that data — Salesforce is designated system of record for the relationship data instead.

questions.q: Why did Carrow's architect recommend External Objects via Salesforce Connect instead of copying balance data into custom Salesforce objects?
options: Copying the data would create an authoritative-copy risk and a synchronization problem at scale; External Objects surface the live data without storing a duplicate
External Objects are required by financial regulation in all cases
Custom objects cannot store currency fields
External Objects are faster to query than any custom object regardless of data volume
questions.explain: Replicating balance data into Salesforce would risk advisors treating a possibly-stale copy as authoritative and would require ongoing synchronization at 340,000 clients' scale — External Objects avoid both by surfacing the core platform's live data without ever storing a Salesforce copy.

questions.q: Why does Carrow's architect recommend a Big Object for compliance-review history older than the current active review cycle?
options: Because Big Objects are required by financial-services regulation
Because the volume of required-retention compliance records would eventually create a large-data-volume performance risk if kept entirely in a standard object
Because Big Objects allow editing of historical compliance records
Because compliance records do not need to be retained under financial regulation
questions.explain: Years of required-retention compliance history across 2,200 advisors and 340,000 clients would grow into a volume that slows down a standard object's day-to-day queries; a Big Object keeps that history queryable but outside the active object's footprint.

questions.q: In this case study, why is client identity data treated as a separate master-data question from account-balance data, even though both originate in the same core banking platform?
options: Identity data and balance data always have the same master in every architecture

Identity data is a compliance and advisor-trust risk if it mismatches between systems, which is a distinct concern from transactional balance accuracy, so it gets its own explicit master-data decision and sync process
Because Salesforce cannot store a client's name or address
Because identity data changes more frequently than balance data
questions.explain: A client identity mismatch (wrong address, wrong tax ID) creates a different kind of risk than a balance discrepancy — it is specifically a compliance and trust problem — which is why this case study treats it as its own master-data decision with a documented sync and correction process, distinct from the balance/transaction system-of-record decision.

questions.q: What risk does explicitly naming which system is authoritative for which data, in writing, specifically head off?
options: The risk of advisors treating a convenient but possibly stale copy of data as authoritative, leading to a real financial conversation based on wrong numbers
The risk of Salesforce running out of storage
The risk of regulators auditing the wrong company
The risk of advisors having too little access to client data
questions.explain: Without an explicit, written system-of-record decision, advisors tend to gravitate toward whichever copy of the data is easiest to read — which is exactly the failure mode that leads to a client conversation driven by a stale or lagging number instead of the regulator-audited source.
